water_bottle: I pour water into the dish. It's already full of rain. I've upgraded a birdbath.
energy_drink: I'm not pouring BULL RUN into a satellite dish. The pigeons are jumpy enough.
rainwater_can: The can's already full. So is the dish. We've reached equilibrium.

LOOK.text: A three-metre bowl of rainwater. The best-funded birdbath in the city.
It also runs a full Base node via satellite. Adrian's birdbath has better uptime than I do.

USE.text: I nudge the dish. A speaker crackles, then reads out block numbers. From orbit. Adrian gets his news from space.

TALK.text: I speak into the dish. My voice goes up to orbit. A satellite leaves me on read.

PICK.text: Bolted to concrete. I'd need a crane, a permit and a much bigger pocket.

OPEN.text: I open the access panel. Cables, an amplifier, and a label: 'Uptime: 847 days.' Longer than any job I've had.

CLOSE.text: I close the panel. The dish goes back to staring at the sky. It's good at it.

PUSH.text: I push the dish. Something beeps unhappily. I push it back. Rule one: never touch production.

PULL.text: I pull a loose cable. The dish hums angrily. I plug it back in and whistle innocently.

GIVE.text: The dish wants a clear sky and nobody touching it. We have that in common.

antenna: I try to put the antenna back. It won't stay. It's tasted freedom.

LOOK.text: A cluster of antennas. Most are bolted tight, but one looks loose. It wobbles like it's had a few.

USE.text: I extend an antenna. It picks up FM radio. 'Never Gonna Give You Up.' Even the roof is rickrolling me.

TALK.text: The antennas crackle. Somewhere in the static, a taxi dispatcher asks for car nine. Car nine never answers.

then.text: I already took the loose one. The array leans a little now. Like it's missing a friend.

else.text: I grab the loose antenna and wiggle it free. Still gets two bars. Could be useful.
SIGNAL BOOST — Salvaged the rooftop antenna

OPEN.text: I open the junction box. A nest of cables. Someone wired this in the dark. Or angry. Or both.

CLOSE.text: I close the junction box. Out of sight, out of my problems.

PUSH.text: I push a tall antenna. It sways and springs back. It's been through worse wind than me.

then.text: I already pulled the loose one free. The rest are firmly mounted.

else.text: I pull the loose antenna free. Still gets two bars. Not bad for salvage.
SIGNAL BOOST — Salvaged the rooftop antenna

GIVE.text: I wave at the antennas. They're receiving, not accepting.

LOOK.text: Stars above, city lights below. Somewhere out there someone is buying a memecoin at 3 AM. Godspeed.

USE.text: I take a photo of the stars. My phone saves a black square. It's a very honest phone.

TALK.text: I whisper to the stars: 'Seen Adrian?' They twinkle. Witnesses always twinkle when they don't want to talk.

PICK.text: I reach for a star. I get a handful of cold air and a moth. The moths followed me up here.

OPEN.text: The sky is already open. It's the one thing in this house without a lock.

CLOSE.text: I can't close the sky. I checked for a hatch. Old habit.

PUSH.text: I push at the sky. The wind pushes back harder. I let it win.

PULL.text: I try to pull the stars closer. Light-years politely decline.

GIVE.text: I give the night sky a moment of silence. It gives me one back. Nice night for it.

then.text: The Bitcoin vane, pointing straight down. The cable to the hatch is slack. Very bearish.
Greased with pizza. It smells like a Friday night. It might actually turn now.

else.text: A weather vane shaped like the Bitcoin logo. A cable runs from its base to the service hatch.
Rusted solid. It needs grease. A lot of grease.

then.text: The vane is already locked pointing down. I can still hear the mechanism clicking beneath the roof.

else.text: I grip the Bitcoin weather vane and force it straight down. Something mechanical clicks beneath the roof — a hidden latch releasing.
The vane locks into position with a heavy clunk. That sound came from the service shaft. The vane must be connected to its locking mechanism.

then.text: The vane is already locked pointing down. I can still hear the mechanism clicking beneath the roof.

else.text: I grip the vane and heave. Nothing. Rusted solid. I've pulled something, and it isn't the vane.

TALK.text: I ask the vane where Adrian went. It creaks and points nowhere. Same answer as everyone else.

PICK.text: It's bolted to a pole. I'd need tools and a reason. I have neither. Yet.

OPEN.text: A tiny compartment in the base. Empty. Somebody got here first. Story of my career.

CLOSE.text: I close the compartment. The vane squeaks. I choose to hear that as 'thank you'.

then.text: I push the weather vane. It creaks and swings back east. The cable to the hatch stays slack — still unlatched.

else.text: I push the weather vane. It creaks and swings back east. *CLUNK* — a cable pulls a mechanical latch beneath the roof. The service shaft hatch!

then.text: I push the weather vane. It creaks and swings west. Bearish sentiment. The cable to the hatch stays slack — still unlatched.

else.text: I push the weather vane. It creaks and swings west. *CLUNK* — a cable pulls a mechanical latch beneath the roof. The service shaft hatch!

then.text: The vane is already locked pointing down. I can still hear the mechanism clicking beneath the roof.

else.text: I push the vane. The vane pushes back. Rust wins.

then.text: I pull the weather vane back east. The cable to the hatch stays slack — still unlatched.

else.text: I pull the weather vane back east. *CLUNK* — a cable pulls a mechanical latch beneath the roof. The service shaft hatch!

then.text: I yank the weather vane west. Bears in control. The cable to the hatch stays slack — still unlatched.

else.text: I yank the weather vane west. *CLUNK* — a cable pulls a mechanical latch beneath the roof. The service shaft hatch!

then.text: The vane is already locked pointing down. I can still hear the mechanism clicking beneath the roof.

else.text: I pull. The rust holds. A muscle I didn't know I had files a complaint.

GIVE.text: The vane doesn't take bribes. It only takes wind. Very principled for a piece of tin.

then.text: The light below is dark now. Whatever the weather vane was connected to, turning it cut the power to this light. Interesting.

else.text: A light blinks rhythmically from below the building. The basement. Something is still running down there. It seems connected to the weather vane's circuit.
That blinking is a server heartbeat. The service hatch goes down there. Of course it does.

USE.text: The light is far below, at ground level. I can't reach it from up here.

then.text: I shout toward where the light was. Darkness doesn't shout back. Good manners, at least.

else.text: I shout toward the light. The blinking pauses. Then carries on. I've been ignored by a bulb.

PICK.text: It's several floors down. My arms are average length. Disappointingly so.

OPEN.text: The light's coming from the foundations. Opening those is a job for the hatch, not me.

CLOSE.text: Too far to close. And I want to know what's blinking down there.

PUSH.text: I lean over the edge. My knees vote no. Unanimously.

PULL.text: I can't pull it from up here. It's doing a good job of pulling me, though.

then.text: The light's off. Darkness doesn't take gifts. It takes keys.

else.text: The light doesn't want anything. Except, apparently, a visit.

LOOK.text: The city glimmers below. Thousands of lights. Most of them are people who forgot the bathroom.

USE.text: I zoom in on the skyline. A neon sign: 'EXCHANGES OPEN 24/7.' That's not a feature. That's a warning.

TALK.text: 'Hey, city! Seen a guy called Adrian?' A car horn honks. I'll take that as a no.

PICK.text: I can't pick up a city. I can barely pick up after myself.

OPEN.text: The city's always open. That's its problem, according to my landlord.

CLOSE.text: Cities don't close. Pharmacies do. Usually right before I get there.

PUSH.text: I push the air toward the city. The city doesn't notice. Cities never do.

PULL.text: I beckon the city closer. It stays put. Stubborn, cities.

GIVE.text: The city takes enough already. Rent, parking, my dignity.

_default: The hatch has a card reader. That isn't a card.
I press it against the hatch. The reader blinks red. Unimpressed.
The hatch wants to see some ID. That isn't ID. That barely counts as stuff.
pizza_slice: Grease the hatch? The hatch isn't rusty. It's paranoid. Something else up here is rusty.
code_note: No keypad on this hatch. 7314 stays in my pocket. The hatch wants a card and a key.

then.text: The hatch hangs open. A ladder drops into the dark, toward the blinking.

else.text: Three locks: a card reader, a keyhole, and something mechanical underneath. Adrian trusts nobody.

then.text: All three are open. After you, me.

else.text: Still shut: the mechanical latch. Its cable runs up to the weather vane.

then.text: Still shut: the keyhole.

else.text: Still shut: the keyhole and the mechanical latch.

then.text: Still shut: the card reader.

else.text: Still shut: the card reader and the mechanical latch.

then.text: Still shut: the card reader and the keyhole.

else.text: All three are shut. Obviously.

then.text: Back down the ladder. Mind the rungs.

then.text: I'm not closing it. Three locks took me long enough.

else.text: Already closed and locked. Three times over.

PUSH.text: I push the hatch. Solid metal. Adrian doesn't do casual visitors.

PULL.text: I pull at the edge. My fingers slip. The hatch has done this before.

GIVE.text: The hatch doesn't take gifts. It takes a card, a key and a turned vane. It's very particular.

LOOK.text: A concrete parapet. Low enough to lean on. High enough to keep detectives on the roof. Mostly.

USE.text: I lean on the railing and survey the city. Wind in my hair. I'd look great on a book cover.

TALK.text: 'What have you seen from up here?' The concrete keeps quiet. Best witness I've had all week.

PICK.text: I chip off a piece of concrete. It crumbles. I put the crumbs back. Nobody saw.

OPEN.text: Parapets don't open. That's the whole point of a parapet.

CLOSE.text: Nothing to close. The parapet works nights. No breaks, no complaints. Penny would hire it.

PUSH.text: I push the railing. Solid. Whoever built this didn't want lawsuits.

PULL.text: I pull the railing. A tiny crack appears. I let go and pretend I was stretching.

GIVE.text: The parapet doesn't want anything. Except me on this side of it. Fair.

keycard: No reader on the roof door. It's just a door. I'd forgotten those exist.

LOOK.text: The door back to the trading floor. Warm light leaks out underneath. Inside sounds nice right now.

TALK.text: The door creaks in the wind. It wants to go back inside. Same.

PICK.text: I'm not taking a door. I've got a hatch to worry about.

CLOSE.text: It's closed. The wind would slam it anyway. The wind has a temper up here.

PUSH.text: I push through the door and head back down.

PULL.text: I pull the door. Warm air rushes out. The roof sighs with envy.

GIVE.text: Doors don't take gifts. DOORIS taught me that the hard way.

LOOK.text: A glass hatch in the roof. Below: the lobby, dim and empty. A ladder runs down the inside.

USE.text: I lift the hatch and climb down the ladder into the lobby.

TALK.text: I call down through the glass. Nobody answers. Penny would answer. Penny would file it.

PICK.text: It's hinged to the roof. It opens. It doesn't come with me.

OPEN.text: I pull the hatch open and descend into the lobby.

CLOSE.text: Already closed. Flush with the roof. Someone was proud of that.

PUSH.text: I push. It opens upward. I've been pushing the wrong way my whole life.

PULL.text: I pull the hatch open and lower myself into the lobby.

GIVE.text: The hatch doesn't want gifts. It wants a pull.

then.text: The reader's already green. It likes Adrian's face. One of us should.

else.text: Beep. Green light. The reader thinks I'm Adrian. It's not the first to make that mistake.

else.text: I rub the slice all over the pivot. The rust drinks it like it's been waiting.
Adrian's diet finally contributes to the infrastructure.

then.text: I already took my share. The pigeons are watching.

else.text: I dip the can in the dish. Rainwater, filtered through a satellite node. Artisanal.
